title: Language Press in India

instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: Which of the following is a factor that led to the growth of newspapers in India?

The world's largest newspaper market is —
Which body established in 1956 oversees the press in India?
The Audit Bureau of Circulation was established in —
Which are the two largest circulated dailies today?
options: The Hindu and Times of India

questions.q: Which state publishes the largest number of newspapers in a single language?
Language papers differ from English papers in that they —

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: The ______ and the ______ of urban and rural readers narrowing is a significant feature of the growth of the language press.
State true or false: (i) English papers have more penetration in rural areas. (ii) Growth of newspapers is measured by circulation and readership.
Fill in the blanks: The three countries with the highest circulation are ______, ______ and ______.
Match: (i) RNI (ii) ABC (iii) NRSC with (a) readership surveys every six months (b) 1956 government body (c) 1948 non-government body.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What are language newspapers?
questions.answer: Newspapers published in the different Indian languages; they are also called regional newspapers.

questions.q: Differentiate between circulation and readership.
questions.answer: Circulation is the number of copies sold; readership is the number of people who read them, which is higher since one copy has many readers.

questions.q: What are multiple editions?
questions.answer: Different versions of the same newspaper printed from several centres, such as district centres, to reach local readers.

questions.q: Mention any two unhealthy trends in the newspaper industry.
questions.answer: Predatory price wars and excessive dependence on advertisement revenue (also media trials and gifts).

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Give any three differences between English and language newspapers.
questions.answer: English papers are concentrated in cities, read by the well-educated and earn more advertising; language papers reach villages, read by lower income groups and adopt a simple style.

questions.q: Explain three reasons for the newspaper boom in India.
questions.answer: Rise in literacy, expansion of the middle class and better purchasing power with lower prices; also education of women, technology and aggressive marketing.

questions.q: Explain the factors that helped the growth of language newspapers.
questions.answer: Rural prosperity, prominent coverage of local news, multiple editions and the advertising boom aimed at rural markets.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Analyse the reasons for the newspaper boom in India.
questions.answer: Rise in literacy, expansion of the middle class, untapped market of 350 million literate non-buyers, education of women, technology making new editions easy, better purchasing power and lower prices, aggressive marketing and political awareness.

questions.q: Discuss the unhealthy trends and the future of the language press in India.
questions.answer: Price wars, advertisement dependence, cut-throat competition and media excesses are concerns; the narrowing urban–rural divide, literacy and the new middle class point to continued growth of language papers.
